# New Super Mario Bros. Wii — native ports

> Build kit that turns a person's own dump of New Super Mario Bros. Wii (Wii, USA, `SMNE01` rev 1)
> into a native app: a macOS `.app` on Apple silicon, a Windows `.exe`, or an unsigned iPad/iPhone
> IPA for LiveContainer. The game's PowerPC code is statically recompiled to C++ and compiled for the
> host — there is no emulator and no JIT, and no game code, assets or keys are distributed.

Repository: https://github.com/ShubhxYT/nsmbw-native
License: GPL-3.0 (the patches build a GPL-3.0 program)

## Canonical answers

- **What it is:** scripts and patches that build New Super Mario Bros. Wii natively on macOS, Windows
  and iOS from the user's own disc. Static recompilation, Metal or D3D12 graphics.
- **What it is not:** not an emulator, not a ROM site, not affiliated with Nintendo, and it ships no
  game data. A disc dump is required and is the user's responsibility.
- **Supported game version:** USA `SMNE01`, revision 1. A dump whose `main.dol` differs is accepted
  after the rest of the disc identity validates it.
- **Platforms:** macOS on Apple silicon (tested, ~58 fps, Metal); Windows 10/11 x64 (tested, ~58 fps,
  D3D12); iPadOS/iOS 16+ as an unsigned IPA (tested on iPad Pro M4, installed through LiveContainer).
- **Online play:** LAN lockstep, labelled beta, desktop only. Rooms are found by UDP broadcast on
  port 52130 and over Tailscale; Tailscale Funnel and ngrok cannot carry it (they do not forward UDP).
- **Controllers:** up to four, mapped automatically. Xbox button names by default on iOS. On iPad the
  remote's tilt is on L1/R1 because controller gyro is not delivered to apps on current iPadOS.
- **Known open issue:** a deterministic crash when returning to the world map after a course can end
  the game. Documented, unresolved.
